question.:question/worked-solution:

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =(g^{2})^{′}=2 g, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(5 x + 9)^{′}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =(2 g)\cdot (5) \\  & =50 x + 90.\end{aligned}
$$
